about: What Shree-Lipi's own composers write for Unicode Punjabi (Gurmukhi): S8PunU64.dll (Unicode) and S8Pun764.dll (Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes), Shree-Lipi nxt, typed the same keys into both (capture r3\cap-pun, 2026-10-18: 12 vendor keyboards and 1,242 probe keyboards, every capture run twice, byte-identical). Each row: the Unicode string, the preferred bytes (hex, one byte per glyph code) and, when there are any, the other spellings the composer also accepts. Canonical typing order only (the i-sign struck first, every other sign after its letter, bindi/tippi/visarga/addak after the sign, subjoined ੍ਰ ੍ਹ ੍ਵ ੍ਯ with their own codes, nukta letters as letter + nukta); the other orders and the composer's quirks are kept in the capture, not here. One choice: a virama before a letter with no subjoined form is preferred as the visible halant B5 (10 of the 12 vendor keyboards put the halant code on their virama key); the link spelling, with no glyph for the virama, stays accepted. Unicode text spells a tippi after ਾ ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ ਉ ਊ ੳ as the bindi and ੱ + ਂ as ਁ, as the Unicode composer writes them. The bytes are SHREE-PUN7-0951/0952 codes; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-PUN-0950/0951/0952/0955/0956 draw the same codes, except ₹ 3C, which they lack (the shree-pun456 tables pass ₹ through, reported). tools/PunTruth builds and checks the shree-pun7 / shree-pun456 tables against it.
